☼The Sunday Spotlight☼

What a Reassessment Actually Does to Your Tax Bill
Every property in North Tonawanda is about to get a new number on it, and Dunkirk is in the middle of its own assessment fight. Here is what all of that means, for people who have never had to think about it before.
What is happening, in both cities. North Tonawanda's council voted 4–1 to reassess all 14,600 parcels and hired GAR Associates for $550,000 to do it. The last full look was 2009; the average house here is assessed at $291,000 today. Ninety minutes down the lake, Dunkirk has been arguing about the same thing from the other end — a court ruled this week in favor of city assessor Erica Munson. Two cities, one problem: what a property is worth on paper versus what it would actually sell for.
The thing almost everyone gets wrong. A reassessment is not a tax increase. The city decides separately how much money it needs — that is the levy, and it is set in the budget. The assessments only decide how that total gets divided up. When every assessment goes up, the tax rate comes down to match, because the same pile of money is being collected from bigger-looking numbers. If every property in the city rose by exactly the same percentage, nobody's bill would change at all.
So why does anyone care? Because properties never move by the same percentage. Seventeen years is a long time, and neighborhoods drift apart. In a reassessment, the winners and losers are decided by how far your property moved relative to everyone else's. Go up less than the city average and your bill goes down. Go up more and your bill goes up. The commercial numbers show how wide that spread can be: the Walmart on Niagara Falls Boulevard is currently assessed at $224,000 a year and could land at just over a million. Every dollar that shifts onto a parcel like that is a dollar that comes off the houses.
Why cities let it go so long. Because it is politically miserable. Somebody's bill always goes up, and that person calls. The cost of waiting is that the drift compounds — and a resident who has been quietly overpaying since 2009 has been subsidizing a neighbor the whole time without either of them knowing it.
What to actually do. When the notice arrives, it will list a proposed assessment, not a tax bill; do not multiply it by the old rate and panic. Check whether the number is roughly what the house would sell for today — that is the only question that matters. If it is too high, there is an informal review with the assessor before anything is final, and that conversation is far easier than the formal grievance that comes later. Bring comparable sales. Grievance Day in New York is the fourth Tuesday in May.
Worth watching both. Dunkirk is the argument after the fact; North Tonawanda is the argument about to start.

🍂The Turning🍂

Still no percentage for the three counties — the next report comes Wednesday afternoon, and it is the first one likely to carry a number for Western New York.
What changes things is the cold. Nothing above 67 all week and lows in the high forties is exactly the pattern that starts the maples turning, so the Wednesday report should finally have something to say. North Tonawanda usually peaks the last week of October.

Tonight Saturn rises in the east at 7:53. Jupiter comes up at 3:30 a.m. Two days to the equinox, Tuesday at 10:05 a.m., when day and night divide evenly and then the dark side wins until March.
Aries
Mercury and Saturn are three degrees from exact opposition, the closest they come. Saturn has sat in your sign all year making you the one who says the hard practical thing; today someone says the opposite across the table. This is the peak of it. Tomorrow it starts to loosen. Kaylani, Luka
Cancer
Mars is in the final degrees of Cancer, still sextile the Sun. It leaves your sign this week and will not be back for two years. Whatever it has been fueling — and you know what it has been fueling — gets one more push and then you are on your own. Gregg
Leo
Mercury sextile Jupiter holds a second day, and Jupiter sits at seventeen degrees of your sign. Two days of the same helpful angle usually means the useful conversation is the one you have already started, not a new one. Follow it up. Leah, Tommy
Virgo
The Sun leaves your sign Tuesday morning at 10:05, at the equinox. Forty-eight hours of Virgo season left. The birthdays are past, the lists are mostly done, and the year hands the wheel to Libra, who will want to talk about it. Derek, Joanne
Scorpio
Venus in Scorpio squares Pluto in Aquarius for a third day, and the Moon in Capricorn has moved off. What is left is the plain version of the aspect: you want something and someone else has a say in it. Negotiate rather than push. Ariel, Claire, Garret

✶The National Wire✶

1

BRICS Marks Twenty Years in New Delhi

The bloc's eighteenth summit opened over the weekend on the twentieth anniversary of its founding, with expansion and dollar-alternative payment systems on the agenda.

2

White House Pulls Its ICE Nominee

The nomination of Lance Schroyer to lead the agency was withdrawn. Separately, ICE has stopped publishing data on miscarriages among women in its custody.

3

Fifteen Years Since Occupy

Activists marked the anniversary of the encampment in the Financial District this week. The phrase “the one percent” outlived the movement by some distance.

☑The Ballot☑

The Three House Seats
Forty-four days. Yesterday's paper covered the governor's race and the A.I. ads; today, the three congressional seats this family votes in. All 26 of New York's House seats are up, along with all 213 in the state legislature, the Attorney General and the Comptroller.
NY-26 — North Tonawanda. Tim Kennedy, Democrat, defending against Republican Dennis Hannon, a software engineer and former bank executive. Buffalo-centered and heavily Democratic; not on anyone's list of competitive races.
NY-23 — Dunkirk. Nick Langworthy, the Republican incumbent and former state party chairman, against Democrat Aaron Gies, a college professor. The 23rd is the most Republican district in New York.
NY-25 — Scottsville. Joe Morelle, Democrat, against Monroe County legislator Virginia McIntyre. Morelle has held the Rochester seat since 2018.
None of the three is expected to be close, which is the honest thing to say and also the reason the statewide races matter more here than the congressional ones. The competitive New York seat is in the Hudson Valley — Mike Lawler against Cait Conley — one of roughly twenty toss-ups nationally that decide the House.
Early voting Oct 24–Nov 1 · register by Oct 24 · Election Day Nov 3.

★The Marquee★

1

Sheeran Played Philadelphia Alone, and Said Something

His first show since the walkout — no openers, no Beoga, just him and the loop pedal at Lincoln Financial Field. From the stage he told the crowd that what is happening in Gaza is “catastrophic and unjustifiable,” and that he is used to his music being criticized. He has said the decision to drop Macklemore was not his; the promoter, Messina Touring Group, says venues told them they would not host shows featuring him, which would have cancelled dates for hundreds of thousands of ticket holders.

2

Macklemore Gives Away the Money

He pledged his entire net earnings from the tour — about a million dollars — to Palestinian relief. He had been booked for eight of the ten remaining dates, including Gillette Stadium on the 25th and 26th, the venue whose owner asked for his removal.

3

Donna Summer, Songwriter

Inducted posthumously into the Songwriters Hall of Fame — late recognition that she wrote or co-wrote most of what she sang.

🏈The Gridiron🏈

Jets and Packers, One O'Clock
Bills · idle. Buffalo is 2–0 and hosts the Chargers next Sunday at one. The long week after a Thursday night game is the best rest on any schedule, and they earned it.
Jets · Green Bay at the Meadowlands, 1:00. New York is 1–0 off a game in which it ran thirty-nine times and held the ball thirty-nine minutes. Breece Hall and Kenyon Sadiq are good to go. Green Bay is 0–1, short across the interior line, without Micah Parsons and without Josh Jacobs, and still favored by about two to one. That is the game.

⚑The Chase⚑

Logano Steals Bristol
Joey Logano went past Ty Gibbs, Carson Hocevar and Kyle Larson with eight laps left to take it — his third win of the year and a surprise. Gibbs and Hocevar got too aggressive with each other on the final restart, and Hocevar and Ryan Blaney ended up in a fight on pit road afterward. Larson's late pass for second put him one point ahead of Denny Hamlin at the top of the Chase; Logano is third, sixteen back, with the top six inside fifty-two points. Kansas next Sunday at three.

✶The Week Ahead✶

Weather. Cool and grey Monday through Wednesday, nothing above 64. Thursday and Friday turn sunny in the mid-60s, and Saturday reaches 70 — the last warm day in sight.
The equinox is Tuesday at 10:05 a.m. After that the nights are longer than the days until March.
Football. Jets and Packers today at one. Bills host the Chargers next Sunday at one.
Racing. Kansas next Sunday at three, race four of ten.
The Turning. New foliage report Wednesday afternoon — the first one likely to put a number on Western New York.
Calendar. Saturday the 26th: the Harvest Moon, full at 12:48 in the afternoon, and the Monroe County harvest festival at Northampton Park the same day.

What is the longest you have ever waited for something, and was it worth it?
Send it to the group chat this week. Answers run here next Sunday under your names.

☾On This Day☾

September 20, 1973 — Billie Jean King beat Bobby Riggs in straight sets in front of 30,000 people in the Astrodome and about 50 million on television. She was 29, he was 55, and he had spent months telling anyone who would listen that he would win.
